154:         Array of reference notes time intervals (onset and offset times)
155:     est_intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(m,2)
156:         Array of estimated notes time intervals (onset and offset times)
157:     """
158:     # If reference or estimated notes are empty, warn
159:     if ref_intervals.size == 0:
160:         warnings.warn("Reference notes are empty.")
161:     if est_intervals.size == 0:
162:         warnings.warn("Estimated notes are empty.")
163: 
164:     # Validate intervals
165:     util.validate_intervals(ref_intervals)
166:     util.validate_intervals(est_intervals)
167: 
168: 
169: def match_note_offsets(
170:     ref_intervals,
171:     est_intervals,
172:     offset_ratio=0.2,
173:     offset_min_tolerance=0.05,
174:     strict=False,
175: ):
176:     """Compute a maximum matching between reference and estimated notes,
177:     only taking note offsets into account.
178: 
179:     Given two note sequences represented by ``ref_intervals`` and
180:     ``est_intervals`` (see :func:`mir_eval.io.load_valued_intervals`), we seek
181:     the largest set of correspondences ``(i, j)`` such that the offset of
182:     reference note ``i`` has to be within ``offset_tolerance`` of the offset of
183:     estimated note ``j``, where ``offset_tolerance`` is equal to
184:     ``offset_ratio`` times the reference note's duration, i.e.  ``offset_ratio
185:     * ref_duration[i]`` where ``ref_duration[i] = ref_intervals[i, 1] -
186:     ref_intervals[i, 0]``. If the resulting ``offset_tolerance`` is less than
187:     ``offset_min_tolerance`` (50 ms by default) then ``offset_min_tolerance``
188:     is used instead.
189: 
190:     Every reference note is matched against at most one estimated note.
191: 
192:     Note there are separate functions :func:`match_note_onsets` and
193:     :func:`match_notes` for matching notes based on onsets only or based on
194:     onset, offset, and pitch, respectively. This is because the rules for
195:     matching note onsets and matching note offsets are different.
196: 
197:     Parameters
198:     ----------
199:     ref_intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(n,2)
200:         Array of reference notes time intervals (onset and offset times)
201:     est_intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(m,2)
202:         Array of estimated notes time intervals (onset and offset times)
203:     offset_ratio : float > 0
204:         The ratio of the reference note's duration used to define the
205:         ``offset_tolerance``. Default is 0.2 (20%), meaning the
206:         ``offset_tolerance`` will equal the ``ref_duration * 0.2``, or 0.05 (50
207:         ms), whichever is greater.
208:     offset_min_tolerance : float > 0
209:         The minimum tolerance for offset matching. See ``offset_ratio``
210:         description for an explanation of how the offset tolerance is
211:         determined.
212:     strict : bool
213:         If ``strict=False`` (the default), threshold checks for offset
214:         matching are performed using ``<=`` (less than or equal). If
215:         ``strict=True``, the threshold checks are performed using ``<`` (less
216:         than).
217: 
218:     Returns
219:     -------
220:     matching : list of tuples
221:         A list of matched reference and estimated notes.
222:         ``matching[i] == (i, j)`` where reference note ``i`` matches estimated
223:         note ``j``.
224:     """
225:     # set the comparison function
226:     if strict:
227:         cmp_func = np.less
228:     else:
229:         cmp_func = np.less_equal
230: 
231:     # check for offset matches
232:     offset_distances = np.abs(
233:         np.subtract.outer(ref_intervals[:, 1], est_intervals[:, 1])
234:     )
235:     # Round distances to a target precision to avoid the situation where
236:     # if the distance is exactly 50ms (and strict=False) it erroneously
237:     # doesn't match the notes because of precision issues.
238:     offset_distances = np.around(offset_distances, decimals=N_DECIMALS)
239:     ref_durations = util.intervals_to_durations(ref_intervals)
240:     offset_tolerances = np.maximum(offset_ratio * ref_durations, offset_min_tolerance)
241:     offset_hit_matrix = cmp_func(offset_distances, offset_tolerances.reshape(-1, 1))
242: 
243:     # check for hits
244:     hits = np.where(offset_hit_matrix)
245: 
246:     # Construct the graph input
247:     # Flip graph so that 'matching' is a list of tuples where the first item
248:     # in each tuple is the reference note index, and the second item is the
249:     # estimated note index.
250:     G = {}
251:     for ref_i, est_i in zip(*hits):
252:         if est_i not in G:
253:             G[est_i] = []
254:         G[est_i].append(ref_i)
255: 
256:     # Compute the maximum matching
257:     matching = sorted(util._bipartite_match(G).items())
258: 
259:     return matching
260: 
261: 
262: def match_note_onsets(ref_intervals, est_intervals, onset_tolerance=0.05, strict=False):
263:     """Compute a maximum matching between reference and estimated notes,
264:     only taking note onsets into account.
265: 
266:     Given two note sequences represented by ``ref_intervals`` and
267:     ``est_intervals`` (see :func:`mir_eval.io.load_valued_intervals`), we see
268:     the largest set of correspondences ``(i,j)`` such that the onset of
269:     reference note ``i`` is within ``onset_tolerance`` of the onset of
270:     estimated note ``j``.
271: 
272:     Every reference note is matched against at most one estimated note.
273: 
274:     Note there are separate functions :func:`match_note_offsets` and
275:     :func:`match_notes` for matching notes based on offsets only or based on
276:     onset, offset, and pitch, respectively. This is because the rules for
277:     matching note onsets and matching note offsets are different.
278: 
279:     Parameters
280:     ----------
281:     ref_intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(n,2)
282:         Array of reference notes time intervals (onset and offset times)
283:     est_intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(m,2)
284:         Array of estimated notes time intervals (onset and offset times)
285:     onset_tolerance : float > 0
286:         The tolerance for an estimated note's onset deviating from the
287:         reference note's onset, in seconds. Default is 0.05 (50 ms).
288:     strict : bool
289:         If ``strict=False`` (the default), threshold checks for onset matching
290:         are performed using ``<=`` (less than or equal). If ``strict=True``,
291:         the threshold checks are performed using ``<`` (less than).
292: 
293:     Returns
294:     -------
295:     matching : list of tuples
296:         A list of matched reference and estimated notes.
297:         ``matching[i] == (i, j)`` where reference note ``i`` matches estimated
298:         note ``j``.
299:     """
300:     # set the comparison function
301:     if strict:
302:         cmp_func = np.less
303:     else:
304:         cmp_func = np.less_equal
305: 
306:     # check for onset matches
307:     onset_distances = np.abs(
308:         np.subtract.outer(ref_intervals[:, 0], est_intervals[:, 0])
309:     )
